traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 288 Lythraceae: herbs, rarely shrubby; leaves opposite or whorled, rarely alternate; stipules none or very small; flowers usually regular (Cuphea irregular); sepals joined in a tube with the petals at its top (read as a hypanthium); petals crumpled in bud; ovary superior, of 2 to 6 cells; fruit usually a capsule. APG adds the woody crape myrtle, pomegranate (inferior ovary, a berry-like fruit) and Sonneratia: so woody as often (Library 1.0's family is about a third trees and shrubs), and the inferior ovary and berry as rare (inferred).
